subtype: Approach: yearly themes with quarterly goals [Action]
passage:
I'm Anand, and looking back, the plan that worked for me was boringly simple. I gave each year a theme. Year one: core skills. Year two: owning one part of the product. Year three: helping others learn it. And so on.
Then every quarter I set one or two goals I could actually measure, like "ship two fixes without review comments" or "write one design note." At the end of each quarter I wrote a short note: what I did, what I missed, what I'd change. My mentor Akash read the notes.
I missed about a third of the goals. But the notes showed me clearly that I was moving, and that made the missed ones feel less like failure.
— Anand

qa.a: Akash, Anand's mentor, read the notes.

qa.q: How did Anand feel about missed goals because of the notes?
qa.a: Anand felt encouraged rather than discouraged, since the notes showed steady movement and made the missed goals feel less like failure.

qa.q: What could Anand change if a quarter's goals are missed repeatedly?
qa.a: Anand could shrink the goals or ask Akash what is getting in the way, and adjust the next quarter.

qa.q: How might Akash have seen the quarterly notes?
qa.a: Akash saw a clear record of what Anand did and missed, which makes it easier to give useful advice.

grounding: The reflection shows a yearly theme with quarterly measurable goals and a short written note each quarter to review them.

passage:
Manager's note, one-to-one, 5 January.
Deepak came to today's one-to-one with a single printed page I had not asked for. Across the top: five years, each with a theme. Year 1, core skills. Year 2, own a module. Year 3, lead small projects. Years 4 and 5 left loose on purpose.
Under this year he had written only two goals for the first quarter: finish the backend certification by 31 March, and fix twenty bugs in the payments module to learn it. At the bottom was a box: 'Quarter review, 3 lines: what I did, what I didn't, what I'll change.'
I asked why so few goals. He said last year he wrote twelve and finished none. I've put a review slot in both our calendars for early April.
Amandeep

qa.q: What were Deepak's two goals for the first quarter?
qa.a: Finish the backend certification by 31 March, and fix twenty bugs in the payments module to learn it.

qa.q: Why did Deepak choose so few goals, and what does that suggest he felt about last year?
qa.a: Last year he wrote twelve and finished none, so he likely felt discouraged and chose fewer goals he could actually meet.

qa.q: What else could Deepak add to the three-line review?
qa.a: He could add a line on what help he needs from Amandeep, so blocks are cleared before the next quarter.

qa.q: How might Amandeep see Deepak's page?
qa.a: Amandeep sees an employee taking ownership of growth without being asked, and backs it by booking the April review.

grounding: It shows a manager's note on an employee who sets yearly themes with one or two measurable goals per quarter, reviewed in a short written note.

31 March, late.
Quarter review, as promised to myself. Year one theme: get solid at data engineering basics. This quarter's goals were two:
1. Finish the SQL and pipelines course. Done, 12 March.
2. Build one pipeline at work end to end without help. Half done. Kalyani had to fix my scheduling part.
What I didn't do: the extra side project. Good, it was never a goal.
What I'll change next quarter: goal 1, finish the pipeline alone, with Kalyani reviewing, not rescuing. Goal 2, present it at the team demo in June.
The five-year sheet stays taped inside my wardrobe. Year two, own the reporting module. Year three, lead something small. I don't know years four and five yet, and that's fine.
Thomas

qa.q: When did Thomas finish the SQL and pipelines course?
How does Thomas feel about not knowing years four and five?
qa.a: Thomas feels calm and accepting about it, content to plan the near years clearly and leave the far ones open.

qa.q: What else could Thomas do to make the June demo goal likely?
qa.a: Thomas could book a practice run with Kalyani a week before the demo, so the presentation isn't rushed.

qa.q: How might Kalyani be affected by the change from rescuing to reviewing?
qa.a: Kalyani gets to guide rather than do the work, which saves Kalyani time and shows how Thomas is growing.

grounding: It shows a person with a yearly theme and one or two measurable quarterly goals reviewing them in a short written note.
